newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Romatex shares dive on bid announcement.
newsitem.headline: Romatex shares dive on bid announcement.

text.p: Shares in Romatex Ltd lost over a third of their value in heavy trading on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) early on Thursday after the textile company said any bid for it would be at less than 330 cents a share.
At 0820 GMT shares had slumped 185 cents or 33.6 percent to 365 cents, just off their worst level for the morning of 350 cents. Some 37,800 shares changed hands in the first hour of trade.
Dealers and analysts said shareholders had been bailing out of the stock following the cautionary announcement.
"People are getting rid of the shares as quickly as they can and trying to bring the price in line with the 330 cent level mentioned by Romatex," one dealer said.
Another said: "A lot of buy orders have been cancelled this morning."
Shares in Romatex have surged this week following news that the country's biggest textile company, Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd (Confram), was weighing a takeover.

Romatex and its parent C.G. Smith Ltd said in a joint statement on Thursday that any bid would be implemented at a price below the market price of 330 cents per ordinary share which was the price ruling on the JSE at the close of business last Friday.
Analysts expressed surprised at the low bid price, saying a price of between seven and eight rand had been seen as reasonable for a Romatex share.
"I cannot think of any good reason why C.G. Smith would want to sell at that level (330 cents)," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"A lot of guys piled into the share speculating that a sale would be at a much higher price," the analyst said.
Dealers said there were also rumours on the market that talks between Romatex and Confram, confirmed earlier this week by Romatex managing director Mike Hankinson, were now off.
"There are so many rumours going round but we have hear that the deal is off...And that this is coming from the Romatex side," a dealer said.
Executives for the companies involved could not be reached for comment on Thursday morning.
